title: Psalms Chapter 87 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 87 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 87 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 87.

questions.question: In Psalms 87, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: His foundation is in the holy mountains.
The LORD loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.
A Psalm or Song for the sons of Korah.
questions.correctAnswer: A Psalm or Song for the sons of Korah.
questions.explanation: The first statement in Psalms 87 is 'A Psalm or Song for the sons of Korah.' which is found in Psalms 87:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD love more than all the dwellings of Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: The gates of Zion
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.' found in Psalms 87:2.

questions.question: What is said about the city of God in Psalms 87?
options: It is built on holy mountains.
It is loved by the LORD.
Glorious things are spoken of thee.
questions.correctAnswer: Glorious things are spoken of thee.
questions.explanation: The text specifically states, 'Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.' found in Psalms 87:3.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm attributed to in Psalms 87?
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Korah
questions.explanation: The chapter is identified as 'A Psalm or Song for the sons of Korah.' in Psalms 87:1.

questions.question: What is the foundation of the subject in Psalms 87?
questions.correctAnswer: The holy mountains
questions.explanation: The text states that 'His foundation is in the holy mountains.' which is found in Psalms 87:1.

questions.question: What term describes the gates of Zion in Psalms 87?
questions.correctAnswer: Loved
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion...' found in Psalms 87:2.

questions.question: What does the chapter declare about the city of God?
options: It is a place of worship.
Glorious things are spoken of it.
It is a city of peace.
questions.correctAnswer: Glorious things are spoken of it.
questions.explanation: The text states that 'Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.' which is found in Psalms 87:3.

questions.question: Which phrase indicates the love of the LORD in Psalms 87?
options: His foundation is in the holy mountains.
Glorious things are spoken of thee.
The LORD loveth the gates of Zion.
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD loveth the gates of Zion.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.' found in Psalms 87:2.

questions.question: What does Psalms 87:3 refer to when mentioning glorious things?
questions.correctAnswer: The city of God
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.' specifically refers to the city of God in Psalms 87:3.

questions.question: What is the primary subject of Psalms 87?
questions.correctAnswer: The city of God
questions.explanation: The chapter focuses on the city of God, particularly in Psalms 87:3 where it states, 'Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God.'

questions.question: What does Selah indicate in Psalms 87?
questions.correctAnswer: A pause for reflection
questions.explanation: The term 'Selah' typically indicates a pause for reflection on the preceding verses, as shown in Psalms 87:3.

questions.question: True or False: The foundation mentioned in Psalms 87 is in the holy mountains.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states 'His foundation is in the holy mountains.' found in Psalms 87:1.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD loves all the dwellings of Jacob as much as the gates of Zion.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob as stated in Psalms 87:2.

questions.question: True or False: Glorious things are spoken of the gates of Zion.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text specifically states that glorious things are spoken of the city of God, not the gates of Zion, as found in Psalms 87:3.

questions.question: True or False: The Psalm is attributed to the sons of David.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Psalm is attributed to the sons of Korah, as stated in Psalms 87:1.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 87 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 87 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which nations are mentioned in Psalms 87:4 as being noted by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Rahab and Babylon
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:4 states, 'I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 87:6 promise will happen if the LORD writes up the people?
options: He shall count that this man was born there
He will judge them according to their works
He will bless them with prosperity
He will give them a new name
questions.correctAnswer: He shall count that this man was born there
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:6 says, 'The LORD shall count, when he writeth up the people, that this man was born there.' It promises recognition of those born in Zion.

questions.question: According to Psalms 87:5, who will establish Zion?
questions.correctAnswer: The highest himself
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:5 states, 'and the highest himself shall establish her,' referring to Zion's establishment by the highest.

questions.question: How do Psalms 87:4 and Psalms 87:5 together emphasize the significance of Zion?
options: By mentioning foreign nations and then asserting Zion's establishment by the highest
By describing Zion as a place of exile and captivity
By comparing Zion to other cities like Babylon and Rahab
By commanding the people to leave Zion for other lands
questions.correctAnswer: By mentioning foreign nations and then asserting Zion's establishment by the highest
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:4 mentions foreign nations, while Psalms 87:5 declares that the highest will establish Zion, highlighting its divine importance.

questions.question: What practical lesson about identity and belonging can believers learn from Psalms 87:4 mentioning diverse nations?
options: God recognizes and includes people from many nations in His plan
Only one nation is favored by God
Believers should avoid association with foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: God recognizes and includes people from many nations in His plan
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:4 lists various nations, indicating God’s inclusive recognition of many peoples.

questions.question: How does Psalms 87:5 encourage believers regarding their spiritual security?
options: Assures that the highest will establish Zion, symbolizing divine protection
Warns that Zion is vulnerable to enemies
States that human efforts alone secure Zion
Says that only certain people will be accepted in Zion
questions.correctAnswer: Assures that the highest will establish Zion, symbolizing divine protection
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:5 affirms that 'the highest himself shall establish her,' giving assurance of God's protective power.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'this man was born there' in Psalms 87:4 imply about the people mentioned?
options: They are considered as natives or belonging to Zion spiritually
They are foreigners who are excluded
They are rulers of other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They are considered as natives or belonging to Zion spiritually
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that those from Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia are counted as born in Zion, indicating spiritual inclusion (Psalms 87:4).

questions.question: Why might the Psalmist include nations like Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia in Psalms 87:4?
options: To demonstrate God's sovereignty over all nations and inclusion of diverse peoples
To show that these nations were enemies
To suggest that these nations should be destroyed
To indicate geographical boundaries of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To demonstrate God's sovereignty over all nations and inclusion of diverse peoples
questions.explanation: Including these nations illustrates God’s universal sovereignty and acceptance beyond Israel (Psalms 87:4).

questions.question: What does Psalms 87:6 teach about God’s record-keeping in relation to His people?
options: God counts and records those born in Zion, affirming their identity
God only records kings and priests
God counts people by their wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God counts and records those born in Zion, affirming their identity
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:6 says the LORD counts in His book those born in Zion, confirming their belonging.

questions.question: How can believers apply the assurance from Psalms 87:5 about the highest establishing Zion to their personal faith journey?
options: Trust that God’s power secures their spiritual foundation despite challenges
Depend solely on human strength for security
Ignore spiritual growth and focus on material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Trust that God’s power secures their spiritual foundation despite challenges
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:5 encourages trust in God’s establishment and protection of Zion, applicable to personal faith.

questions.question: In light of Psalms 87:4-6, what role does remembrance or mention by God play for believers?
options: It affirms their identity and inclusion in God’s covenant people
It is irrelevant to their faith
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms their identity and inclusion in God’s covenant people
questions.explanation: Mention in God’s record (Psalms 87:4-6) affirms belonging and blessing for those counted in Zion.

questions.question: How does the love for the gates of Zion in Psalms 87:2 relate to the identity of those born there in Psalms 87:4-6?
options: God’s love for Zion emphasizes the value of those counted as born there
God’s love excludes those not born there
The gates symbolize physical defense only
questions.correctAnswer: God’s love for Zion emphasizes the value of those counted as born there
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:2’s love for Zion’s gates underlines the special status of those born there, as described in verses 4-6.

questions.question: What does the mention of 'this man was born there' in Psalms 87:5 and 87:6 suggest about God’s view of spiritual lineage?
options: God considers spiritual birth in Zion as true identity regardless of ethnic origin
Only physical birth in Zion counts
God favors only one family line
questions.correctAnswer: God considers spiritual birth in Zion as true identity regardless of ethnic origin
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase shows that God regards those counted as born in Zion as truly belonging to Him (Psalms 87:5-6).

questions.question: How can the inclusiveness shown in Psalms 87:4 inspire Christian prayer and mission?
options: By motivating believers to pray for and include all nations in God’s kingdom
By focusing prayer only on their own community
By emphasizing isolation from other peoples
questions.correctAnswer: By motivating believers to pray for and include all nations in God’s kingdom
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:4’s mention of various nations encourages inclusive prayer and mission efforts.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 87:1 indicates that the foundation of Zion is in the holy mountains.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:1 says, 'His foundation is in the holy mountains,' confirming this statement.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 87 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 87.

questions.question: According to Psalms 87:7, who shall be present in Zion?
options: As well the singers as the players on instruments
Only the kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: As well the singers as the players on instruments
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:7 specifically states, 'As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there,' indicating both groups are present.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'all my springs are in thee' in Psalms 87:7 metaphorically refer to?
questions.correctAnswer: Source of life and blessing
questions.explanation: The phrase 'all my springs are in thee' in Psalms 87:7 metaphorically refers to Zion as the source of life and blessing for the psalmist and the community.

questions.question: In Psalms 87:7, what is the relationship between the singers and the players on instruments?
options: Only players on instruments shall be there
questions.correctAnswer: Both shall be there
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:7 states 'As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there,' indicating both groups are included.

questions.question: The phrase 'all my springs are in thee' in Psalms 87:7 can be best understood as illustrating which theological concept?
options: God as the source of sustenance and blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God as the source of sustenance and blessing
questions.explanation: The phrase 'all my springs are in thee' (Psalms 87:7) symbolizes that God or Zion is the source of life, sustenance, and blessing, a common theological theme in the Psalms.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the tone of Psalms 87:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Celebratory and confident
questions.explanation: The verse expresses confidence and celebration of Zion’s role as the source of life and worship, as seen in Psalms 87:7.

questions.question: How does Psalms 87:7 connect to the broader theme of the chapter?
options: It affirms Zion as the spiritual and cultural center
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Zion as the spiritual and cultural center
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:7, emphasizing singers and players on instruments and the springs being in Zion, culminates the chapter’s theme that Zion is the foundation and spiritual center.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'מַעְיָן' (ma‘yan) in Psalms 87:7 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Spring or fountain
questions.explanation: 'מַעְיָן' (ma‘yan) in Psalms 87:7 literally means 'spring' or 'fountain,' referring to a source of water and metaphorically to a source of life.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 87:7 where 'singers' and 'players on instruments' are mentioned together?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:7 uses parallelism by pairing 'singers' and 'players on instruments' to emphasize the completeness of worship, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s people coming from many nations as mentioned in Psalms 87:4-5?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 7:9
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:9 describes a great multitude from every nation, tribe, and people, reflecting Psalms 87:4-5's theme of diverse nations associated with Zion.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse connects with Psalms 87:2’s declaration of the LORD loving the gates of Zion more than all dwellings of Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 62:10
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:10 speaks of preparing the way for the people and lifting up the gates of Zion, connecting with the special love for Zion’s gates expressed in Psalms 87:2.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Psalms 87:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 87:6
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:6 precedes verse 7 and sets the context with 'The LORD shall count, when he writeth up the people...,' leading into the presence of singers and musicians in verse 7.

questions.question: How does Psalms 87:7 function as a typology in biblical worship practices?
options: It anticipates the full assembly of worshipers and musicians in the temple
It prophesies destruction of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the full assembly of worshipers and musicians in the temple
questions.explanation: The verse’s mention of singers and players on instruments anticipates the ideal worship assembly seen later in temple worship, typifying complete praise.

questions.question: Which literary structure is evident in the first two verses of Psalms 87, highlighting Zion’s foundation and God's love for its gates?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:1-2 forms an inclusio framing the psalm by mentioning Zion’s foundation and God's love for its gates, creating thematic bookends.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 87:7 states that only instrumental players shall be present in Zion, excluding singers.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:7 explicitly states 'As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there,' including both groups, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 87:2 declares that the LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:2 clearly states, 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob,' making the statement true.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 87 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 87 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 87:2 teach about God's nature?
options: God's special love for Zion above all dwellings of Jacob
God's universal impartiality among all nations
God's wrath against the dwellings of Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: God's special love for Zion above all dwellings of Jacob
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:2 explicitly states that 'The LORD loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob,' demonstrating God's particular love and favor for Zion.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 87:4 teach about the inclusion of nations in God's people?
options: God acknowledges birth and belonging of foreigners in Zion
Only ethnic Israelites can belong to God's people
God excludes nations like Babylon and Ethiopia from salvation
God's covenant is restricted to the sons of Korah only
questions.correctAnswer: God acknowledges birth and belonging of foreigners in Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:4 mentions Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia, stating 'this man was born there,' indicating that people from foreign nations are recognized as belonging to Zion.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 87:5 teach about the establishment of Zion?
options: The Highest Himself will establish Zion
Zion is established by human effort
Zion is an ephemeral city with no divine foundation
The establishment of Zion depends on the kings of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Highest Himself will establish Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:5 declares 'and the highest himself shall establish her,' emphasizing that God's sovereign action secures Zion's foundation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:6 states that 'The LORD shall count, when he writeth up the people, that this man was born there,' showing God's all-knowing attribute as He records every individual born in Zion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:1 says 'His foundation is in the holy mountains,' indicating God's nature as holy and His dwelling in a sanctified place.

questions.question: How does Psalms 87 contribute to the biblical narrative arc of God's kingdom?
options: It anticipates the inclusion of Gentile believers into the people of God
It restricts God's kingdom to ethnic Israel exclusively
It describes the destruction of Zion as a judgment
It emphasizes the temple's physical construction over spiritual realities
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the inclusion of Gentile believers into the people of God
questions.explanation: By mentioning nations like Babylon and Ethiopia in Psalms 87:4 as being 'born' in Zion, the psalm prefigures the New Testament theme of Gentiles being grafted into God's people (cf. Romans 11:17-24).

questions.question: How does Psalms 87:7 prepare for the eschatological worship in the New Testament?
options: By depicting all singers and players gathered in Zion, it envisions universal worship
By focusing solely on Levitical singers, it excludes Gentiles
By portraying silence in Zion, it suggests the end of worship
By emphasizing instrumental worship over vocal praise
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting all singers and players gathered in Zion, it envisions universal worship
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:7 states 'As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there,' symbolizing inclusive, joyous worship that anticipates eschatological praise (cf. Revelation 5:9-13).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 and 5 teach about God's relationship to Zion?
options: God's sovereign love establishes Zion and identifies its citizens
God's love for Zion is conditional on human merit
Zion's establishment is independent of God's will
God's relationship to Zion is purely symbolic with no real effect
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign love establishes Zion and identifies its citizens
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows God's love for Zion, and verse 5 states that 'the highest himself shall establish her,' together teaching that God's sovereign love both establishes Zion and marks its people as His own.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 4 and 6 teach about divine election and belonging?
options: God records and acknowledges the birth of individuals from diverse nations as chosen citizens of Zion
God limits election strictly to Israelite ethnicity
God's election is random and unrecorded
Belonging to Zion is based on geographic residence only
questions.correctAnswer: God records and acknowledges the birth of individuals from diverse nations as chosen citizens of Zion
questions.explanation: Verse 4 mentions foreign nations whose people are 'born there,' and verse 6 states God 'shall count, when he writeth up the people,' indicating divine election includes diverse nations and is meticulously recorded.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 and 7 teach about the nature of Zion and worship?
options: Zion is the holy foundation where continual joyful worship flows from God’s springs
Zion is a temporary dwelling with limited worship
Worship in Zion is silent and somber due to its holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Zion is the holy foundation where continual joyful worship flows from God’s springs
questions.explanation: Verse 1 describes Zion as 'His foundation in the holy mountains,' and verse 7 mentions singers and players with 'all my springs are in thee,' portraying Zion as the sacred source and place of vibrant worship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 87:4-6 teaches exclusivism by naming only certain nations as belonging to Zion. What does Psalms 87:4-6 actually teach?
options: It teaches inclusion of diverse peoples into God's people, not exclusivism
It teaches that only those nations named have salvation
It restricts salvation to ethnic Israelites alone
It denies any foreigners can belong to Zion
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches inclusion of diverse peoples into God's people, not exclusivism
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 mention nations like Rahab (Egypt), Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia as places of birth for God's people, affirming inclusion rather than exclusivism.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 87:3 teach about God's city and His promises?
options: Glorious things are spoken of the city of God, highlighting the certainty of God's promises to Zion
God’s city is temporary and insecure
God’s promises to Zion are conditional and uncertain
Zion is portrayed as insignificant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Glorious things are spoken of the city of God, highlighting the certainty of God's promises to Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 87:3 says, 'Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God,' conveying the certainty and majestic nature of God's promises regarding Zion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusiveness
questions.explanation: Verse 4 lists foreign nations whose peoples are acknowledged as born in Zion, demonstrating God's inclusive nature toward the nations.

questions.question: How does Psalms 87:5-6 connect to the New Testament doctrine of the Church as the people of God?
options: It anticipates the divine registration and establishment of all believers as citizens of God's city
It limits God's people to ethnic Israel only
It rejects any notion of a spiritual community
It teaches that birthright is purely physical and unimportant
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the divine registration and establishment of all believers as citizens of God's city
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 speak of God establishing Zion and counting those born there, foreshadowing the New Testament teaching of believers being born into God's spiritual family and recorded in heaven (cf. Philippians 3:20).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 and 7 teach about worship and divine presence in Zion?
options: Glorious and joyful worship flows from God's presence in Zion
Worship in Zion is minimal and lacking joy
God's presence is absent from Zion
Worship is confined to silent meditation only
questions.correctAnswer: Glorious and joyful worship flows from God's presence in Zion
questions.explanation: Verse 3 highlights the 'glorious things' spoken of Zion, while verse 7 mentions singers and instruments and 'all my springs are in thee,' symbolizing vibrant worship flowing from God's presence.
